record.original_question: For an equational theory E and an ordering greater-than, is there a set of inference rules that always succeeds in computing a convergent set of rewrite rules R whenever such an R exists for the ordering, even when the ordering cannot be made total on ground terms?

evidence.quote: Is there a set of inference rules that always succeeds in computing a convergent set of rewrite rules for a given set of equations and an ordering, provided that it exists?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E$ be a set of equations over a set of terms built from a signature $\mathcal{F}$ and variables, and let $>$ be a reduction ordering on terms (i.e., a well-founded strict ordering that is closed under contexts and substitutions). A rewrite system $R$ is said to be convergent (with respect to $>$) if every rule $\ell \to r \in R$ satisfies $\ell > r$, if $R$ is confluent, and if its equational theory coincides with that of $E$ (so that every $E$-equivalence class has a unique $R$-normal form). 

Question: Does there exist a set of inference rules for completion that, given any equational theory $E$ and any reduction ordering $>$ for which some convergent rewrite system $R$ contained in $>$ presenting $E$ exists, is guaranteed to compute such an $R$? In particular, must the procedure succeed even when $>$ cannot be extended to a reduction ordering that is total on ground terms?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to have been resolved by Bofill, Godoy, Nieuwenhuis, and Rubio, whose work on "Paramodulation and Knuth–Bendix Completion with Nontotal and Nonmonotonic Orderings" introduced a new completeness proof technique requiring only well-foundedness and the subterm property, and produced a Knuth–Bendix completion procedure that finds a convergent term rewriting system for a given set of equations and a (possibly non-totalizable) reduction ordering whenever such a system exists.

status_evidence.title: Paramodulation and Knuth–Bendix Completion with Nontotal and Nonmonotonic Orderings
status_evidence.snippet: All existing completeness results required term orderings to be totalizable on ground terms; the authors give a new technique requiring only well-foundedness and the subterm property, yielding the first KB completion procedure that finds a convergent TRS for a given set of equations and a (possibly non-totalizable) reduction ordering whenever it exists.
status_evidence.claim: A completion procedure exists that succeeds whenever a convergent rewrite system exists for the given (possibly non-totalizable) reduction ordering.
